experiences.name: Teotihuacan Pyramids & Street Food
experiences.description: Visit the ancient pre-Aztec city of Teotihuacan, climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Moon, and on the way back stop at local roadside stalls for barbacoa tacos and pulque, a traditional fermented agave drink.
experiences.location: Teotihuacan, State of Mexico (day trip from CDMX)

experiences.name: Coyoacán Neighborhood & Frida Kahlo Museum
experiences.description: Wander the cobblestone streets of bohemian Coyoacán, visit the iconic Casa Azul (Frida Kahlo Museum), browse the weekend artisan market, and enjoy a traditional Mexican lunch at a local fondita.

experiences.name: Taco Crawl in La Condesa & Roma
experiences.description: Self-guided evening taco crawl through two of CDMX's trendiest neighborhoods. Sample al pastor from a trompo, suadero, and carnitas at legendary street stands, paired with agua fresca or a cold cerveza.
experiences.location: La Condesa & Colonia Roma, Mexico City

experiences.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes & Historic Center Walk
experiences.description: Admire the stunning Art Nouveau exterior of Bellas Artes, explore the Diego Rivera murals inside, then walk through the Zócalo, visit the Metropolitan Cathedral, and tour the Templo Mayor ruins — a deep dive into Mexican history and art.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Use this time to rest on the plane and prepare your arrival checklist.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at AICM airport at 13:00. Take the Metro Line 5 from Terminal 1 (or authorized airport taxi for ~$8-10 USD) to your hotel in Centro Histórico. Check in, freshen up, then take a relaxed orientation stroll around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución) — one of the largest city squares in the world. Admire the Metropolitan Cathedral and the National Palace facades from outside (both free to view externally). Get your bearings and soak in the vibrant street atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the pedestrian street Madero, lined with street performers and vendors. Visit the Palacio de Bellas Artes exterior illuminated at dusk (free). Wind down with dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport.
meals.lunch: Grab affordable tacos or quesadillas from a street stall near the Zócalo (~$2-4 USD). Try tacos de canasta or tacos al pastor.
meals.dinner: El Cardenal (Centro branch) for traditional Mexican cuisine — budget-friendly set menu comida corrida for ~$6-8 USD, or explore nearby fondas (family-run restaurants) on Calle Mesones for even cheaper options (~$4-6 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Keep your luggage light and use the Metro for airport transfer (Line 5, ~$0.25 USD) to save money. Avoid exchanging currency at the airport — use a local ATM in Centro for better rates. Stay aware of your surroundings as you settle in.

day_by_day.morning: Start early at the Zócalo to beat the crowds. Visit the Templo Mayor archaeological site and museum (~$4 USD) — the ancient Aztec temple ruins right in the heart of the city. Spend 1.5-2 hours exploring the excavated ruins and the museum's impressive collection of artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the National Palace (Palacio Nacional) — FREE entry. Marvel at Diego Rivera's stunning murals depicting Mexican history covering the entire main staircase and upper floor. Afterward, explore the historic streets of Centro Histórico: Calle Regina, a charming pedestrian street, and the nearby Mercado de San Juan for artisan goods and local snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Plaza Garibaldi (15-min walk or short Metro ride) to hear Mariachi bands perform in the open square — a quintessential Mexico City experience. Grab a beer or mezcal from a surrounding cantina and enjoy the live music atmosphere. Return safely to the hotel via Metro or Uber.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local fonda near the hotel — chilaquiles or huevos rancheros with coffee (~$3-5 USD). Look for a 'Desayuno Corrido' sign.
meals.lunch: Tacos or tortas from street vendors near Templo Mayor (~$2-3 USD), or sit-down comida corrida at a nearby fonda for a full meal (~$4-6 USD).
meals.dinner: Pozole or tacos at a casual restaurant near Plaza Garibaldi, or grab antojitos (street snacks like tlayudas, sopes, gorditas) from market stalls (~$3-5 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays — perfectly timed for Tuesday. The National Palace is free but may require showing ID. Plaza Garibaldi is lively and safe in the early evening but exercise caution late at night. Consider taking an Uber back to the hotel after dark.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro Line 2 to Bellas Artes station. Visit the Palacio de Bellas Artes interior (~$1.50 USD) to see Diego Rivera, Rufino Tamayo, and David Alfaro Siqueiros murals inside. Then walk to the nearby Museo Franz Mayer (decorative arts museum, ~$3 USD) housed in a stunning colonial building with a beautiful courtyard café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along Avenida Juárez and explore Alameda Central park — a beautiful historic green space, free to enter. Continue to Barrio Chino (Chinatown) on Calle Dolores for a unique cultural detour. Then head to the Mercado de Artesanías La Ciudadela (~20-min walk or short Metro ride) for affordable handicrafts, textiles, and souvenirs — great for browsing even on a budget.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico and visit the rooftop terrace bar at Hotel Downtown Mexico or Gran Hotel Ciudad de México for stunning Zócalo views — order just one drink (~$4-6 USD) to enjoy the panoramic view. Afterward, stroll along the lit-up streets of Centro for a relaxing end to the day.

meals.breakfast: Tamales and atole (corn-based warm drink) from street vendors near Bellas Artes — a classic Mexico City breakfast (~$2-3 USD).
meals.lunch: Comida corrida at a fonda near Alameda Central — a full 3-course meal with soup, main dish, and agua fresca (~$4-6 USD).
meals.dinner: Tostadas and antojitos at Mercado de San Juan Arcos de Belén or a nearby taquería (~$4-6 USD). Try tostadas de tinga or enfrijoladas.

day_by_day.notes: The Palacio de Bellas Artes has free entry on Sundays — if you want to save money, swap this day's plan to Sunday. Franz Mayer museum is closed on Mondays. La Ciudadela market is great for budget-friendly authentic crafts — bargaining is acceptable.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to Xochimilco via Metro + light rail (total ~$1 USD). Rent a trajinera (colorful flat-bottomed boat) with other travelers — shared boats can cost as little as $10-15 USD per hour. Float through the ancient canal network, enjoy marimba music from passing boats, and buy fresh food and drinks from vendors on the water. This is one of Mexico City's most iconic cultural experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit Coyoacán neighborhood (reachable via Metro Line 3 to Viveros or Coyoacán station). Explore the charming cobblestone streets, the central Jardín Centenario plaza, and the famous Mercado de Coyoacán for street food. Visit the exterior of the Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul) — book tickets in advance online (~$10 USD) if budget allows, or simply enjoy the neighborhood's bohemian atmosphere for free.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the lively evening atmosphere in Coyoacán's main square — street performers, local vendors, and a relaxed community vibe. Have dinner here before heading back to Centro via Metro.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick breakfast before leaving — pan dulce (sweet bread) and café de olla from a bakery or street cart (~$1-2 USD).
meals.lunch: Eat on the trajinera in Xochimilco — buy fresh elotes (corn), quesadillas, or snacks from canal vendors (~$3-5 USD).
meals.dinner: Tacos de guisado or enchiladas at Mercado de Coyoacán or a nearby local restaurant (~$4-6 USD). Try the tostadas de pata — a Coyoacán specialty.

day_by_day.notes: Start early for Xochimilco (by 9:00 AM) to avoid weekend crowds (though it's a Thursday). Negotiate the trajinera price before boarding. The Frida Kahlo Museum sells out quickly — book online in advance if you want to go inside. Coyoacán is very safe and walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec — one of the world's greatest museums (~$4.50 USD, free on Sundays). Spend 2-3 hours exploring pre-Columbian civilizations including the Aztec Sun Stone and Maya artifacts. It's a must-see for culture lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Bosque de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Forest) — one of the largest urban parks in the world, completely FREE. Rent a rowboat on the lake (~$3-4 USD), visit the free zoo (Zoológico de Chapultepec), or simply relax on the grass. End the afternoon with a walk through the upscale Polanco neighborhood nearby — window-shop on Presidente Masaryk Avenue and enjoy the contrast with Centro Histórico.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico for a final evening. Visit the Mercado de Artesanías near the Zócalo for any last-minute souvenirs. Enjoy a farewell dinner at a traditional pulquería (pulque bar) — try this ancient fermented agave drink (~$1-2 USD per glass) alongside botanas (free bar snacks). End the night with a final walk around the illuminated Zócalo.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at a local café near the hotel — molletes (toasted bread with beans and cheese) or enfrijoladas (~$3-5 USD).
meals.lunch: Street food near Chapultepec — elotes, tlayudas, or tacos from vendors outside the park (~$3-5 USD), or pack snacks from a nearby OXXO convenience store to eat in the park.
meals.dinner: Traditional farewell dinner at a local pulquería or fonda in Centro Histórico — try mole negro with rice and beans, or a classic caldo de pollo soup (~$5-7 USD). Toast to a great trip!

day_by_day.notes: The Museo Nacional de Antropología is massive — wear comfortable shoes and prioritize the Mexica (Aztec) and Maya rooms if time is limited. Chapultepec Forest is free and perfect for a relaxed afternoon. Keep small bills (pesos) handy throughout the day for street vendors. Begin packing in the evening if departing the next day.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Check in to your boutique hotel in Centro Histórico, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest public squares in the world. Visit the exterior of the Palacio Nacional and the stunning Metropolitan Cathedral. Stroll down Madero Street, a lively pedestrian corridor lined with colonial architecture and street performers.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the illuminated Centro Histórico at dusk — the buildings are beautifully lit at night. Visit the rooftop bar at Gran Hotel Ciudad de México for a panoramic view of the Zócalo with a cocktail in hand.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a coffee and pastry at your hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Head to Café de Tacuba (Calle Tacuba 28), a historic restaurant open since 1912 — try the enchiladas or pozole. Mid-range pricing, great atmosphere.
meals.dinner: El Cardenal (Palacio de Iturbide location) — a beloved local institution serving traditional Mexican cuisine like chiles en nogada and tamales. Budget ~300–500 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Since your flight lands at 13:00, factor in ~45–60 minutes for baggage claim and taxi/metro to Centro Histórico. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel. Use Uber or an authorized airport taxi for safety.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Palacio Nacional to see Diego Rivera's famous murals depicting Mexican history — free entry. Arrive early (opens at 9:00) to beat crowds. Afterward, explore the Templo Mayor archaeological site and its museum, the ruins of the ancient Aztec capital Tenochtitlán, right in the heart of the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Mercado de San Juan (about 15 minutes on foot) — a beloved mid-range food market popular with locals and chefs. Browse gourmet cheeses, charcuterie, fresh seafood, and international specialties. Then visit the Museo de Arte Popular (MAP) nearby to discover vibrant Mexican folk art and crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Barrio Chino (Chinatown) and the surrounding streets of Centro for a different vibe. End the evening with a mezcal tasting at a local mezcalería such as La Botica or Bósforo — both casual, affordable, and authentically Mexican.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy breakfast at your hotel or stop at a local fondita near the Zócalo — try chilaquiles or huevos rancheros for ~80–150 MXN.
meals.lunch: Graze through Mercado de San Juan — pick up tacos de canasta, fresh ceviche, or a torta from the market stalls. Budget ~100–200 MXN.
meals.dinner: Los Girasoles (Calle Tacuba) — refined yet affordable Mexican cuisine in an elegant colonial setting. Try the duck in mole or the cactus salad. ~300–450 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor entry is ~85 MXN and includes the museum. Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll cover a lot of ground today. The Zócalo area can get busy on weekdays; arrive at Palacio Nacional right at opening.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro (Line 3, Hidalgo → Copilco) or an Uber to Coyoacán, a charming bohemian neighborhood about 20–30 minutes from Centro. Visit the Casa Azul — the Frida Kahlo Museum — a deeply personal and culturally rich experience. Book tickets online in advance as they sell out quickly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Coyoacán's colorful streets and visit the Mercado de Coyoacán for snacks and local crafts. Try a tostada de tinga or a quesadilla from the market. Explore the central plaza (Jardín Centenario) and the historic Iglesia de San Juan Bautista. Stop by the León Trotsky Museum nearby for a fascinating slice of 20th-century history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico and explore the Alameda Central park area. Visit the Palacio de Bellas Artes (exterior and lobby are free) to admire the stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture. Check for evening cultural events or concerts — performances are often affordable.

meals.breakfast: Have breakfast at El Jarocho coffee shop in Coyoacán — a legendary local café serving café de olla and pan dulce. Very affordable (~60–100 MXN).
meals.lunch: Eat at the Mercado de Coyoacán — tostadas, enchiladas, or fresh fruit. ~100–180 MXN.
meals.dinner: Azul Histórico (Isabel la Católica 30, Centro) — beautiful courtyard setting, excellent modern Mexican cuisine. Try the mole negro or the fish tacos. ~350–500 MXN per person.

day_by_day.notes: Frida Kahlo Museum tickets must be booked online at museofridakahlo.org.mx — entry is ~270 MXN. Coyoacán is best enjoyed on foot once you arrive. The neighborhood has a very different, quieter energy than Centro — a great contrast day.

day_by_day.morning: Take an Uber or organized tour (~30–40 minutes) to Teotihuacán, the ancient Mesoamerican city with the iconic Pyramids of the Sun and Moon. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun for panoramic views of the ancient city. Explore the Avenue of the Dead and the Temple of Quetzalcóatl. Arrive early (site opens at 9:00) to avoid midday heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City by early afternoon (~2–3 hours at the site is ideal). Head to the Colonia Roma neighborhood — a trendy, artsy district with beautiful Art Nouveau buildings. Browse independent bookshops, galleries, and boutiques along Álvaro Obregón Avenue.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Roma Norte for the evening — one of the city's best neighborhoods for food and nightlife. Explore the vibrant restaurant scene and enjoy a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing — grab a quick torta or tamale from a street stall near your hotel, or eat at the hotel (~80–150 MXN).
meals.lunch: At Teotihuacán, eat at one of the restaurants near the site exit — La Gruta (inside a natural cave) is a memorable mid-range option. ~250–400 MXN per person.
meals.dinner: Contramar (Durango 200, Roma) — a Mexico City institution famous for its tuna tostadas and grilled fish. Lively, casual, and beloved by locals. ~350–550 MXN per person. Reserve ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Teotihuacán entry is ~90 MXN. You can take a public bus from Terminal Norte (Metro Autobuses del Norte, Line 5) for ~50 MXN round trip — budget-friendly alternative to Uber. Wear sunscreen and bring water — the pyramids offer little shade. Book Contramar in advance as it fills up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec — one of the world's greatest museums, home to the Aztec Sun Stone and extraordinary pre-Columbian artifacts. Plan at least 2–2.5 hours; the collection is vast. Located in Bosque de Chapultepec, the city's massive urban park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Chapultepec Park and visit the Castillo de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Castle) — a hilltop palace turned national history museum with sweeping city views. Afterward, walk or take the Metro to Polanco, Mexico City's upscale neighborhood, for window shopping and people-watching along Presidente Masaryk Avenue.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico for a final evening. Pick up last-minute souvenirs at Mercado de Artesanías La Ciudadela (a large crafts market). End the trip with a memorable farewell dinner and a final mezcal toast to Mexico City.

meals.breakfast: Café Nin (Havre 73, Juárez) — a stylish, mid-range café near Chapultepec serving excellent chilaquiles verdes and specialty coffee. ~150–250 MXN.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick, delicious bite in Polanco — try a taco stand or a casual torta shop for ~100–200 MXN, saving room for a special dinner.
meals.dinner: Limosneros (Allende 3, Centro Histórico) — an intimate restaurant near your hotel celebrating pre-Hispanic and regional Mexican ingredients. Exceptional moles and seasonal dishes. ~400–600 MXN per person. A perfect farewell meal.

day_by_day.notes: Museo de Antropología entry is ~90 MXN (free on Sundays for Mexican nationals). Chapultepec Castle entry is ~90 MXN. Both are within the same park — very walkable. La Ciudadela market is open daily and offers some of the best craft prices in the city — great for textiles, talavera pottery, and folk art. Reserve Limosneros in advance for your final evening.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Mexico City International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to boutique hotel in Centro Histórico. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided walking tour of Centro Histórico's UNESCO World Heritage core: explore the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), admire the imposing Metropolitan Cathedral, and visit the Palacio Nacional to see Diego Rivera's legendary murals depicting Mexican history. Stroll through the atmospheric streets of the historic center with your expert local guide.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo hour at the rooftop bar of your boutique hotel or a nearby iconic terrace overlooking the Zócalo. Dinner at Contramar or a comparable upscale Mexico City institution — indulge in refined Mexican cuisine with an emphasis on fresh seafood and traditional flavors in an elegant setting.

meals.lunch: Light welcome snack or room service upon arrival at the hotel
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium Centro Histórico restaurant such as Azul Histórico — traditional Mexican dishes, mezcal cocktails, and a beautiful courtyard ambiance

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after the 13:00 arrival. Pre-arrange a private airport transfer with your hotel concierge. Keep the evening relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Private early-access visit to the Templo Mayor archaeological site and its world-class museum — explore the Aztec ceremonial center at the heart of ancient Tenochtitlán with a specialist archaeologist guide. Afterward, browse the artisan stalls and galleries along nearby República de Uruguay street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private chauffeured transfer to the Museo Nacional de Antropología in Chapultepec — one of the greatest anthropology museums in the world. Spend 2–3 hours with a private guide exploring pre-Columbian civilizations, including the iconic Aztec Sun Stone. Stroll through the lush Bosque de Chapultepec afterward.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktails at Limantour (consistently ranked among the world's best bars) in Colonia Roma. Follow with a tasting-menu dinner at Pujol — Chef Enrique Olvera's flagship restaurant and one of Latin America's top dining destinations, offering an extraordinary modern Mexican tasting experience.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at your boutique hotel — fresh tropical fruits, chilaquiles, and Mexican pastries
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at the Museo Nacional de Antropología's on-site restaurant or a nearby Polanco bistro
meals.dinner: Multi-course tasting menu at Pujol (advance reservation essential) — paired with premium Mexican wines or mezcal selections

day_by_day.notes: Book Pujol well in advance — reservations fill up weeks ahead. Arrange private transport for the Chapultepec trip as it is about 25 minutes from Centro Histórico.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private excursion to the ancient pyramids of Teotihuacán — depart early by private luxury vehicle. Enjoy exclusive early-access entry before the crowds arrive. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon with a private archaeologist guide. Explore the Avenue of the Dead and the Palace of Quetzalpapálotl.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return journey stops at a traditional obsidian artisan workshop for a demonstration and premium souvenir shopping. Optional visit to a local pulque hacienda for a tasting of this ancient fermented agave drink. Arrive back in Centro Histórico by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset mezcal tasting experience at a curated mezcalería in Centro Histórico — guided flight of artisanal single-origin mezcals with expert pairing notes. Dinner at Quintonil (Chef Jorge Vallejo) in Polanco — a celebrated modern Mexican restaurant emphasizing indigenous ingredients and sustainability.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet breakfast at the hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Traditional Mexican lunch at a premium restaurant near Teotihuacán — slow-cooked barbacoa, fresh salsas, handmade tortillas, and regional specialties
meals.dinner: Tasting menu at Quintonil — innovative Mexican cuisine with seasonal, locally sourced ingredients and wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 7:00–7:30 AM for Teotihuacán to beat the heat and crowds. Wear comfortable walking shoes and sunscreen. The round trip is approximately 1.5 hours each way by private car.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive private cooking class with a celebrated local chef — learn to prepare authentic Mexican dishes from scratch: masa-making for tamales and tortillas, mole negro, and seasonal market-fresh salsas. Begin with a guided tour of a traditional mercado (Mercado de San Juan) to select ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the vibrant neighborhoods of Colonia Roma and Condesa by foot or private bicycle — admire the Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture, visit independent art galleries, boutique concept stores, and the beautiful Parque México. Stop for artisan coffee at a specialty café.
day_by_day.evening: Private cultural experience: attend a performance of Ballet Folklórico de México at the stunning Palacio de Bellas Artes — Mexico's premier fine arts venue, a masterpiece of Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture. Pre-show cocktails in the Bellas Artes lobby bar.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a celebrated café in Centro Histórico — café de olla, pan dulce, and fresh-squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes prepared during your morning cooking class — a true farm-to-table experience
meals.dinner: Post-show late dinner at a premium restaurant in Centro Histórico such as El Cardinal — traditional Mexican fine dining with an extensive wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book Ballet Folklórico tickets in advance — performances typically occur on Sundays and Wednesdays. Confirm the schedule and reserve premium seating through your hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning — private guided visit to the Museo Franz Mayer, a stunning 16th-century hospital turned decorative arts museum, featuring one of Mexico's finest collections of colonial furniture, textiles, and ceramics. Stroll through the adjoining cloister garden with a café con leche.
day_by_day.afternoon: Curated luxury shopping experience in the Centro Histórico and nearby Colonia Polanco — visit high-end boutiques, artisan silver jewelers on Calle Madero, premium mezcal and chocolate shops, and designer concept stores. Optional visit to the iconic Casa de los Azulejos (House of Tiles) for a final cultural moment.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sunset cocktails at a panoramic rooftop bar — Torre Latinoamericana observation deck for 360° views of the city skyline. Final celebratory dinner at Dulce Patria (Chef Martha Ortiz) — a theatrical, emotionally charged Mexican fine dining experience blending tradition, art, and haute cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent final breakfast at your boutique hotel — full Mexican spread with eggs al gusto, fresh fruit, tamales, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Leisurely lunch at the iconic Café de Tacuba — a century-old institution in Centro Histórico serving classic Mexican dishes in a beautifully tiled colonial setting
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Dulce Patria — multi-course menu celebrating Mexican culinary heritage with artful presentation and premium cocktail or wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Coordinate checkout and luggage storage with your hotel concierge to enjoy a full final day without interruption. Arrange private transfer to the airport well in advance based on your departure flight time.
